questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The escape velocity from the surface of the Earth is about:
questions.explanation: Escape velocity is √(2GM/R) and does not depend on the mass or direction of projection of the body. The value 7.9 km/s is the orbital velocity near the surface.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The energy stored in an inductor of inductance L carrying a steady current I is:
questions.explanation: Work must be done against the back emf while the current is built up, and this energy is stored in the magnetic field, in the same way ½CV² is stored in a capacitor's electric field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two thin lenses of powers +5 D and -2 D are placed in contact with each other. The focal length of the combination is:
questions.explanation: Powers add, so P = 5 - 2 = +3 D, and f = 1/P = 1/3 m, which is about +33.3 cm. The combination is converging.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 9: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to the (n + l) rule, the orbital filled immediately after 3p in a multi-electron atom is:
questions.explanation: For 4s, n + l = 4 + 0 = 4, while for 3d it is 3 + 2 = 5. The lower sum fills first, which is why potassium and calcium are s-block elements.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 2: Structure of Atom

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The half-life of a zero order reaction is:
options: Directly proportional to the initial concentration
Inversely proportional to the initial concentration
questions.explanation: For a zero order reaction t½ = [A]₀/2k, so doubling the starting concentration doubles the half-life. Only a first order reaction has a concentration independent half-life.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The Hinsberg reagent, benzenesulphonyl chloride, is used to:
options: Distinguish between primary, secondary and tertiary amines
questions.explanation: A primary amine gives a product soluble in alkali, a secondary amine one insoluble in alkali, and a tertiary amine does not react at all.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Mycoplasmas are unusual among prokaryotes because they:
options: Have the thickest cell wall of all bacteria
Completely lack a cell wall and are the smallest living cells known
questions.explanation: Having no cell wall, they are unaffected by penicillin, which works by blocking cell wall synthesis. They can survive without oxygen and cause disease in plants and animals.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In Chargaff's base equivalence rule for double stranded DNA:
options: A + T always equals G + C
The amount of adenine equals that of thymine and guanine equals cytosine
All four bases are present in equal amounts
questions.explanation: This equivalence was a crucial clue to base pairing, and it also means total purines equal total pyrimidines. The A + T to G + C ratio varies from species to species.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Erythroblastosis foetalis can occur when:
options: An Rh negative mother carries an Rh positive foetus in a later pregnancy
An Rh positive mother carries an Rh negative foetus
Both mother and foetus are Rh negative
The mother has blood group O
questions.explanation: The first pregnancy sensitises the mother, and in a later one her anti-Rh antibodies cross the placenta and destroy the foetal red cells. Anti-Rh injections prevent this.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 15: Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following best describes stabilising natural selection?
options: Both extreme forms are favoured over the average
The average or intermediate form is favoured and the extremes are eliminated
Only one extreme form is favoured
Selection has no effect on the population
questions.explanation: Stabilising selection narrows variation and keeps the population as it is, directional selection shifts the mean one way, and disruptive selection favours both extremes.
